results.message: What did Augustine say about Psalm 137, dashing the little ones against the rock?

voice_event.speaker: lpc
voice_event.text: Augustine says the little ones of Babylon are bad desires at their birth, and we must dash them on the Rock, who is Christ: “How shall they repay her? As she has treated us. Let her little ones be choked in their turn. Yes, let her little ones in their turn be dashed, and die. What are the little ones of Babylon? Evil desires at their birth. For some people have to fight with old, deep-rooted cravings. When a craving is born, evil habit has not yet given it strength against you. While it is little, do not let it gain the strength of evil habit. While it is little, dash it. But you fear that, though dashed, it may not die. ‘Dash it against the Rock; and that Rock is Christ.’”. He said this in a sermon on the psalm, and he meant it as teaching for us, not only for that one moment. Babylon, in his reading, is this world in its confusion. Its little ones are the lusts and bad desires just beginning in us. We are to catch them early, while they are still small, and destroy them by dashing them against Christ, the Rock. That is how we crucify our own flesh. The image is violent because the thing itself is hard. The work of killing a desire when it first stirs is real work, and it is ours to do.

names.name: Augustinius of Hippo Regius, presbyter 391, bishop 395/396-430

figures_used.bridge_line: Our bishop at Hippo. The people seized him and brought him to be made a presbyter while he wept. Later they pressed him into the bishop's office over his own refusal. He spent his last days weeping over psalms of penitence, while an army lay outside the walls.

dates.display: converted 386, baptised 387; seized by the congregation at Hippo and ordained presbyter against his own wishes in 391, weeping through it (Possidius, Vita IV); designated coadjutor and consecrated bishop of Hippo by Megalius, primate of Numidia, in 395/396, again amid popular acclamation (Possidius, Vita VIII); died 430, during the Vandal siege of Hippo

confidence.divergence_note: The text field is the NPNF English as printed. Augustine comments on the Latin Psalter, where Psalm 136 ends 'Blessed is he who shall hold and dash thy little ones against the rock'. 'Choked' renders offocentur, 'be smothered', and 'dashed' renders elidantur, 'be struck down'. The closing words echo 1 Corinthians 10:4, which the Latin cites.
